title: The Veil of Ashvale
premise: Rosalind Brightwater, a mercenary bound to the silent god Veyra and keeper of ledgers for the Ashvale Guild of impossible trades, discovers that the fallen border wards and extinguished stars are the work of a crown-entity called the Hollow King—a parasite that has worn the realm's monarch for a generation and now hungers for every memory in the kingdom. Rosalind's own guild ledger holds the key: entries written in the god's hand before its silence, recording how to unmake what wears the crown. Gathering a found family of guild misfits—a memory-thief, a disgraced warden, and a child who remembers the future—Rosalind journeys to the capital as the Hollow King erases the past city by city. In the throne room, Rosalind learns Veyra did not abandon them but was devoured first, and by feeding the god their own most precious memories they rekindle it enough to burn the parasite free. The king dies mortal and forgiven, the stars relight, and Rosalind—half-forgotten but wholly loved—rebuilds the guild not as traders in impossible things, but as keepers of what must be remembered.
about_author: Hazel Almeida is a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing damaged manuscripts before turning to fiction about things that refuse to stay forgotten. She writes at night, keeps meticulous notebooks she claims she never rereads, and lives near a coastline whose lighthouses feature in everything she writes.

chapters.title: The Ledger of Impossible Things
chapters.summary: POV Rosalind. In the Ashvale guildhouse, Rosalind audits a ledger entry for a bottled lullaby while dodging questions from guildmaster Corvane about why their god has gone silent. The chapter establishes the guild's rules: trade fairly, record everything, stay invisible. Emotional beat: quiet unease beneath routine—the sense that invisibility is a debt coming due.

chapters.title: The Night the Stars Went Out
chapters.summary: POV Rosalind. Border wards collapse in a sound like tearing silk; above Ashvale, stars gutter out one by one, leaving constellations blank. Refugees arrive carrying gaps where memories should be. Rosalind's oath-mark burns cold for the first time in years. Emotional beat: dread crystallizing into purpose.

chapters.title: What the Memory-Thief Stole
chapters.summary: POV Sable, a guild thief who steals memories rather than objects. She returns from a job in the borderlands empty-handed and terrified: her client paid her to forget paying her. She brings Rosalind a scrap of stolen royal memory showing a crowned figure with no face. Emotional beat: fear shared becomes alliance.

chapters.title: Corvane's Last Instruction
chapters.summary: POV Rosalind. Guildmaster Corvane reveals he has been hiding pages torn from the god's own ledger—entries describing 'the thing that wears the crown'—then is assassinated by warden-soldiers bearing the king's seal. Dying, he tells Rosalind: 'Unbind him.' Emotional beat: grief transformed into inheritance; Rosalind inherits both the guild and the mission.

chapters.title: The Warden Who Defected
chapters.summary: POV Idris Vale, a border warden who let the wards fall—or failed to stop whoever did. Hunted by his own order, he reaches the guildhouse seeking the only people who might know why. Rosalind offers sanctuary against guild law's better judgment. Emotional beat: distrust tested; the found family gains its reluctant soldier.

chapters.title: A Child Who Remembers Tomorrow
chapters.summary: POV Rosalind. A nameless child arrives at the guild gates speaking of events that haven't happened, including Rosalind standing in a burning throne room. The guild debates sheltering her; Sable reads the child's memories and finds them impossibly intact when everyone else's are fraying. Emotional beat: tenderness amid escalating stakes—the family grows again.

chapters.title: The City That Forgot Its Name
chapters.summary: POV Idris. The party travels toward the capital and finds the river-city of Marrowgate emptied of identity: signs blank, residents smiling and vacant, a town crier announcing nothing. They learn the Hollow King feeds on memory to sustain itself. Emotional beat: horror made intimate as Idris nearly loses his own name.

chapters.title: Entries in the God's Hand
chapters.summary: POV Rosalind. Studying Corvane's hidden pages, Rosalind deciphers Veyra's script: the god once served the first king, and something followed him back from beyond the wards. Unbinding requires a vessel willing to carry divine fire—and to pay for it in memories. Emotional beat: resolve shadowed by cost; Rosalind begins choosing what they might lose.

chapters.title: The Toll Bridge of Small Mercies
chapters.summary: POV Sable. At a bridge guarded by a toll-keeper who charges one true memory per crossing, Sable bargains, cheats, and finally pays honestly—sacrificing her memory of her mother's face so the others cross whole. Emotional beat: sacrifice freely given; the thief gives away the one thing she never stole.

chapters.title: Wardens at the Inn
chapters.summary: POV Idris. Royal wardens corner the party at a mountain inn; Idris faces his former commander and chooses the family over the order, buying their escape with wounds he may not survive. The child's prophecy flickers: 'the soldier falls twice.' Emotional beat: loyalty proven in blood; Idris's guilt begins to burn off.

chapters.title: The Hollow Court
chapters.summary: POV Rosalind. Disguised as ledger-clerks, they enter the capital and witness court life under the Hollow King: nobles reciting borrowed memories, servants without reflections, a palace where yesterday never happened. Rosalind secures an audience by trading an impossible thing—a vial of unspent grief. Emotional beat: uncanny dread sharpening into anger.

chapters.title: The Audience
chapters.summary: POV Rosalind. Face to face with the king, Rosalind feels the parasite notice them—it recognizes Veyra's mark and offers a bargain: serve it, and the god's silence will be explained. Rosalind refuses and barely escapes with Sable's help, learning the entity fears only the ledger pages. Emotional beat: terror and defiance entwined.

chapters.title: What Veyra Never Said
chapters.summary: POV Rosalind. Hiding in the undercity, Rosalind deciphers the final page: Veyra wasn't silent by choice—it was devoured first, and its last act was hiding itself inside its faithful. Rosalind realizes the god lives fragmentarily within every oath-bearer, including themself. Emotional beat: abandonment reframed as love; grief inverted.

chapters.title: The Price of Fire
chapters.summary: POV Sable. The group plans the unbinding: someone must carry Veyra's kindled flame to the crown, paying in their dearest memories. Each member volunteers; Rosalind forbids all but themself. The child quietly tells Sable what Rosalind will forget. Emotional beat: fierce, painful devotion—the family argues like family.

chapters.title: Idris Rises
chapters.summary: POV Idris. Wounded and presumed done, Idris rallies the scattered border wardens who suspect the truth, staging a diversion at the palace gates. He falls once here—as the child foretold—but his wardens hold the line. Emotional beat: redemption earned; the soldier's second fall still waits.

chapters.title: The Throne Room Burns Twice
chapters.summary: POV Rosalind. Fulfilling the child's vision, Rosalind walks into the burning throne room and confronts the Hollow King, offering the bargain of the flame. The parasite accepts, believing it can consume Veyra whole. Emotional beat: calm at the center of catastrophe; Rosalind lies beautifully.

chapters.title: The Unbinding
chapters.summary: POV Rosalind. As the flame takes hold, the Hollow King tears itself free of the dying king, and Rosalind pays the price—memories peeling away like ash even as Veyra roars back to light through them. The god and mercenary burn the parasite out of the world together. Emotional beat: transcendence through loss; climax of theme and plot.

chapters.title: Half-Remembered
chapters.summary: POV Sable. In the aftermath, Rosalind wakes diminished—no memory of their childhood, their oaths' origins, or why Sable weeps holding their hand. The king, freed for one mortal hour, asks forgiveness and receives it before dying human. Emotional beat: bittersweet dawn; victory measured in what remains.

chapters.title: The Stars Relight
chapters.summary: POV Idris. Across the kingdom, memories flood home; in Ashvale, the stars return constellation by constellation. Idris, surviving his second fall after all, carries Rosalind home while the child hums a song no one taught her. Emotional beat: relief and wonder; the long night ends.

chapters.title: Ledger Opened, Ledger Closed
chapters.summary: POV Rosalind. Rosalind formally closes Corvane's ledger and opens a new one, refounding the guild with new laws: remember everything, charge fairly, hide no longer. Veyra speaks faintly through the oath-mark—not commands, just company. Emotional beat: renewal; identity rebuilt on chosen foundations.

chapters.title: What We Keep
chapters.summary: POV Sable. Sable attempts to return her sacrificed memory of her mother's face, kept safe in a stolen locket, but finds she'd rather build new ones—with this family. The child finally shares her name: it belongs to tomorrow. Emotional beat: warmth; found family fully realized.

chapters.title: The Veil of Ashvale
chapters.summary: POV Rosalind. One year later, the guild stands openly in rebuilt Ashvale, taking cases no court will touch—justice outside the law, memory kept sacred. On the anniversary night, Rosalind lights a lamp for everyone the world forgot, and Veyra's mark glows like a small returning star. Emotional beat: peace hard-won; the veil lifts, and they step through it together.
